players.name: Josh Allen
notes: The Keep #1 · average 2.38 across 32 Superflex boards
plus: Seven-board Superflex lock: Keep #1, average 2.0.
Dual-threat floor still separates him from every other aging QB1.
minus: Turns 31 in 2026 — first real dynasty age tax on a perennial 1.01.
Yates PPR has him in the late 20s; 1QB redraft does not pay the SF premium.
grafs: Josh Allen is still the player Ball Keep is built around. Seven sources — PFN, Dynasty Nerds, FantasyPros, KeepTradeCut, and the three X experts we track — all have him inside the top four Superflex assets, and the average lands at 2.0. That is not a recency spike. It is the market admitting that a quarterback who runs, extends, and finishes in the end zone is the safest way to keep a Superflex roster relevant through 2029.

The 2025 tape is the same argument on film: launch-point throws and designed keepers, with the Bills still built to let him create when protection breaks. Redraft boards (Field Yates has him in the high 20s) treat him as a mid QB1 because 1QB leagues do not have to pay the second-starter tax. Dynasty Superflex does. That split is the whole point of The Keep.

The minus is honest: he will be 31 this season, and the first time a 23-year-old passer (Maye) outranks him on a short list, the age conversation gets louder. We are not selling the 1.01 for that. We are naming it. If you are rebuilding past 2028, Maye is the bet. If you are trying to win the next two title windows, Allen is still the chip you do not put in a trade calculator for fun.

players.name: Drake Maye
notes: The Keep #2 · average 2.79 across 32 Superflex boards
plus: FantasyPros ECR, Erickson, and Fitzmaurice all have him SF #1.
Age-23 quarterback who just took New England to an AFC title game.
minus: KeepTradeCut still has him sixth — the market has not fully caught the expert boards.
Yates redraft QB ranking lags the dynasty tape; 2026 weekly floor is not Allen/Lamar yet.
grafs: Drake Maye is the dynasty argument of 2026. Three of our short expert lists (FantasyPros ECR, Andrew Erickson, Pat Fitzmaurice) rank him the Superflex 1.01, Derek Brown has him second, and the long boards (PFN, Dynasty Nerds) park him third behind only Allen. The Keep average is 2.43. That is a 23-year-old passer being priced like a finished product.

The 2025 film is why. The Can't-Miss clip we embedded is the AFC run in miniature: Maye dropping a touchdown and a receiver finishing like a superhero. New England's offense finally looks like a place where a long-striding quarterback can push the ball and scramble without the supporting cast being a weekly apology. Superflex managers who waited on the 2024 draft capital got paid.

The pushback is KeepTradeCut at six and redraft boards that still treat him as a high-end QB2 in 1QB. That is useful. It means you can still find a manager who thinks Allen/Lamar/Hurts are 'safer' and will overpay in picks to move down. Ball Keep's stance: the experts have moved. The startup ADP will follow. Do not be the last one holding the 2024 'he might be Caleb-tier' take.

players.name: Bijan Robinson
notes: The Keep #3 · average 4.38 across 32 Superflex boards
plus: Keep #4 and redraft RB1/RB2 territory in both PPR and standard.
Age-24 workhorse with the receiving chops to survive a negative game script.
minus: Atlanta's supporting cast and game script can cap weekly explosiveness even when the talent is 1.01.
Seven-board average of 5.71 is a hair behind Chase — some SF managers will always take the WR first.
grafs: Bijan Robinson is the running back The Keep is willing to take in the same breath as Chase. Dynasty Nerds have him second overall. Yates has him as a top-two PPR pick. Standard scoring bumps him even further. The 238-yard game we clipped from 2025 is not a meme week; it is the ceiling that makes managers ignore every 'running backs don't last' sermon for one more startup.

What the experts are buying is the complete profile: between-the-tackles power, speed to the edge, and enough routes to keep him on the field on third down. At 24 he is still on the young side of a feature back's prime. That is rare in a 2026 running-back market full of 27-year-old win-now names.

The honest minus is architecture. Atlanta can become a game-script problem, and Superflex drafters who believe Maye/Allen/Chase are less replaceable will let Bijan slide one spot. If you are in 1QB or a redraft league that rewards rushing volume, do not overthink it. He is a first-round pick with a younger age curve than CMC, Henry, or Barkley.

players.name: Ja'Marr Chase
notes: The Keep #4 · average 4.79 across 32 Superflex boards
plus: Consensus WR1 on The Keep (avg 4.0) and a top-six redraft name in both PPR and standard.
2025 tape still shows the tackle-breaking, 60-yard-chunk profile that made him a 1.01 skill player.
minus: Bengals quarterback health is the only real tax — Burrow's availability swings Chase's weekly ceiling.
Erickson has him WR-side at 8, a reminder that some SF boards will take two QBs before any receiver.
grafs: Ja'Marr Chase is the skill-position 1.01 that Superflex has not fully dethroned. Our average of 4.0 across seven boards puts him in the Allen/Maye/Bijan cluster, and Yates still has him as a top-four PPR pick. The 2025 Can't-Miss play — 63 yards of broken tackles — is the scouting report: speed, strength, and a refusal to be brought down by the first or second man.

Where boards disagree is not talent, it is format. Erickson sliding him to eight is a Superflex tell: some experts will take Daniels/Herbert before they take a receiver. That is correct process and still leaves Chase as the first non-QB off most of our sheets. PPR redraft loves him even more than dynasty does, because you do not have to save a slot for a second passer.

The minus is Cincinnati's quarterback room, not Chase. If Burrow misses time, the weekly floor dips and the 'is this still a WR1 week?' tweets start. Dynasty can live through that. Redraft feels it immediately. We are not fading the player. We are fading the injury news cycle around the person throwing him the ball.

Ball Keep's seven-board mix lands him sixth because a few expert lists still stuff quarterbacks in front of every back. That gap is a buying opportunity in startups that use KTC as gospel and a selling opportunity if someone offers you Allen/Maye straight up in Superflex.

The 2025 Eagles game we embedded — 146 yards of burst and cutback — is why scouts stopped calling him a change-of-pace. He is a feature back who happens to be explosive. Detroit will still sprinkle Montgomery into short-yardage, and that is the minus you live with. It has not stopped Gibbs from being a weekly RB1.

Age and efficiency are the dynasty case. The redraft case is even cleaner: PPR and standard both have him in the top two because the Lions keep scoring. If your league mates still think 'Detroit backfield' means a split you cannot trust, let them. Then take Gibbs and stop talking.

minus: Standard scoring taxes him versus PPR (Keep loves him more than STD redraft).
A true WR1 price means you are paying for 2025 being the new baseline, not a spike.
grafs: Jaxon Smith-Njigba is the receiver the industry decided was real in 2025. Ball Keep has him fifth in Superflex, ahead of Gibbs on average, with Brown and Fitzmaurice both inside the top 10. The old 'he's a slot specialist' fade is dead. The 100-yard clip against Pittsburgh is the weekly version: get him the ball in space and let him finish.

Dynasty likes him even more than redraft standard does, which is the tell. PPR captures the volume. Superflex still has to wait until the quarterbacks are gone, but among skill players JSN is in the Chase/Puka/Bijan band. Seattle's offense has become a place where a receiver can put up WR1 weeks without waiting for a once-a-year explosion.

The risk is paying WR1 money for a player whose 2025 might have been the leap rather than the floor. We think it is the floor. If you are a manager still ranking him as a WR2 because of the 2023-24 tape, The Keep is the other side of that trade.

players.name: Jayden Daniels
notes: The Keep #7 · average 7.34 across 32 Superflex boards
plus: Keep #8, seven sources, dual-threat SF QB2/3 on most expert lists.
Erickson has him SF #2 — the loudest young-QB bet besides Maye.
minus: Derek Brown slamming him to 23 is the biggest expert split on The Keep.
Yates redraft ranking in the 40s: 1QB leagues do not have to roster the rushing floor the same way.
grafs: Jayden Daniels is the Superflex argument with the widest expert spread on our sheet. Erickson has him second overall. Brown has him 23rd. Everyone else is in the 6–17 band. Ball Keep averages that into Keep #8, which is our way of saying: we believe the rushing quarterback is a top-10 SF asset, and we are not pretending one cold ranking doesn't exist.

The 2025 deep ball to McLaurin we clipped is the passing-game proof people wanted after the rookie year. Washington can still be a messy supporting-cast week, but the quarterback creating explosives with his legs and his arm is the profile that wins Superflex titles. Maye is the cleaner 'pocket plus' bet for some; Daniels is the 'he can beat you two ways every week' bet.

Redraft 1QB is where the tax shows up. Yates has him outside the top 40 overall because you only start one passer and the weekly floor still swings with protection and drops. If you are drafting Superflex, ignore that board. If you are drafting Yates PPR, wait. The player is the same. The format is not.

notes: The Keep #8 · average 8.62 across 32 Superflex boards

grafs: Puka Nacua's 2025 snow-angle catch is the player in one clip: body control, contested-catch strength, and a quarterback who trusts him when the play dies. Ball Keep has him seventh in Superflex. Yates has him as a top-five PPR pick. That is a receiver who skipped the 'prove it again' year and went straight to alpha usage.

The Keep's source mix loves him because the production is not scheme-dependent gadgetry. He wins inside and outside. He wins in weather. He wins when the Rams need a chunk on third down. Among non-QBs only Chase, Bijan, JSN, and Gibbs are consistently ranked ahead of him on our boards.

The minus is the aging quarterback and a franchise that will eventually have to answer the Stafford question. Dynasty managers who need a five-year WR1 without quarterback risk may prefer Chase or JSN. For 2026 redraft and the next two Superflex windows, Nacua is a first-round name we are not fading on vibes.

Redraft loves the weekly ceiling (Yates in the mid-30s overall is still a QB1 pick). Dynasty has to ask how many more years the rushing volume holds. If you need a two-year window, Lamar is a smash. We are not selling Burrow for a QB2 package. We are not taking him over Maye, Daniels, or Herbert in a startup without a discount. The player is elite. The ranking is a health ranking. That is the whole page.

notes: The Keep #11 · average 12.02 across 29 Superflex boards
plus: Keep #12 on three long boards — Chicago's franchise passer still in the SF top 15.

The Bears have stacked Odunze, Loveland, and Burden around him, which is how you build a five-year passing game even when the weekly box score still looks like a work in progress.

The Can't-Miss scramble from 2025 is both the plus and the minus. Plus: he can still win a down when everything dies. bb_waivers_dynasty.name: Konnor Griffin
bb_waivers_dynasty.why: Post-deadline dynasty add #1. 19-year-old shortstop the TDG board already has inside the overall 30.

bb_waivers_dynasty.name: Jesús Made
bb_waivers_dynasty.why: The model and the prospect lists still agree: stash the 19-year-old if he is free.

bb_waivers_dynasty.name: Walker Jenkins
bb_waivers_dynasty.why: Closer to his peak than Made; RotoGraphs has him just ahead. Rebuilds should not be choosing between them on waivers.

bb_waivers_dynasty.name: Kevin McGonigle
bb_waivers_dynasty.why: The Tigers kid the model stuffed. If he is still sitting, that is a process error.

bb_waivers_dynasty.name: Sal Stewart
bb_waivers_dynasty.why: RotoGraphs 12th overall. If your league is asleep, this is the buy.

bb_waivers_dynasty.name: Nick Kurtz
bb_waivers_dynasty.why: Thumb ding in the model. The talent is still a top-15 dynasty 1B. Stash the IL.

bb_waivers_dynasty.name: Cam Schlittler
bb_waivers_dynasty.why: The pitching-nut add. TDG has him ahead of half the veteran aces.

bb_waivers_dynasty.name: Chase Burns
bb_waivers_dynasty.why: Age-23 arm the Pitcher List crowd is stuffing. Dynasty only.

bb_waivers_dynasty.name: Roman Anthony
bb_waivers_dynasty.why: Boston's young outfield bat. Hold through the September noise.

bb_waivers_dynasty.name: JJ Wetherholt
bb_waivers_dynasty.why: Middle-infield prospect the long boards have inside the 60.

bb_waivers_dynasty.name: Carson Benge
bb_waivers_dynasty.why: Mets outfield flyer. Cheap if your league still treats him as a name.

bb_waivers_dynasty.name: Samuel Basallo
bb_waivers_dynasty.why: Catcher who is not a zero in dynasty. Rare.

bb_waivers_dynasty.name: Payton Tolle
bb_waivers_dynasty.why: Young Red Sox arm. Stash, do not stream.

bb_waivers_dynasty.name: Colt Emerson
bb_waivers_dynasty.why: Mariners shortstop prospect. Deep-league only, still a Keep-adjacent name.

bb_waivers_redraft.name: Tanner Scott
bb_waivers_redraft.why: Diaz is leaking. Scott has the Dodger ninth on ESPN's chart. Saves leagues start here.

bb_waivers_redraft.name: Jordan Romano
bb_waivers_redraft.why: Three saves in a week. Ugly team, real job. Stream the ninth.

bb_waivers_redraft.name: Grant Taylor
bb_waivers_redraft.why: White Sox closer climbing the FantasyPros chart. Available in too many 12-teamers.

bb_waivers_redraft.name: Jacob Webb
bb_waivers_redraft.why: Cubs ninth after Palencia's IL. Priority add in saves.

bb_waivers_redraft.name: Yoendrys Gomez
bb_waivers_redraft.why: Twins saves. Not a committee you ignore in September.

bb_waivers_redraft.name: Riley O'Brien
bb_waivers_redraft.why: If he was dropped after a quiet week, grab him back. 30-save pace.

bb_waivers_redraft.name: Louis Varland
bb_waivers_redraft.why: Blue Jays ninth. SV+H monster even if the closer label wobbles.

bb_waivers_redraft.name: Pete Fairbanks
bb_waivers_redraft.why: Marlins saves are still saves. Streaming weeks matter more than team quality now.

bb_waivers_redraft.name: Cam Schlittler
bb_waivers_redraft.why: Best two-start / rest-of-season streaming ace who is not locked everywhere.

bb_waivers_redraft.name: Drew Rasmussen
bb_waivers_redraft.why: Rays innings. Stream him until he proves you shouldn't.

bb_waivers_redraft.name: Parker Messick
bb_waivers_redraft.why: September starter you can stream twice. Ratios over wins.

bb_waivers_redraft.name: Nolan McLean
bb_waivers_redraft.why: Mets arm with enough Ks to start in a 12-team this week.

bb_waivers_redraft.name: Gavin Williams
bb_waivers_redraft.why: The other Cleveland stream. Two-start weeks first.

bb_waivers_redraft.name: Eury Pérez
bb_waivers_redraft.why: If he is healthy and free, he is not a stream, he is a roster.

bb_waivers_redraft.name: Chase Burns
bb_waivers_redraft.why: Redraft managers still treating him like a prospect. He can help this month.

bb_waivers_redraft.name: Andy Pages
bb_waivers_redraft.why: Dodger playing-time bat. Run this week, not next year.

bb_waivers_redraft.name: Daylen Lile
bb_waivers_redraft.why: Hot bat the model noticed. Stream outfield if you are chasing average.

bb_waivers_redraft.name: Alec Burleson
bb_waivers_redraft.why: Cardinals counting stats. Boring, useful, available.

bb_waivers_redraft.name: Ceddanne Rafaela
bb_waivers_redraft.why: Steals + runs in a playoff push. Redraft candy.

bb_waivers_redraft.name: Tyler Soderstrom
bb_waivers_redraft.why: Power stream at 1B/OF. Athletics lineup still scores enough.

bb_waivers_redraft.name: Jonathan Aranda
bb_waivers_redraft.why: Rays first base. If Kurtz owners need a fill-in, start here.

bb_waivers_redraft.name: Ben Rice
bb_waivers_redraft.why: Yankees catcher/1B eligibility. September volume.

bb_waivers_redraft.name: Hunter Goodman
bb_waivers_redraft.why: Coors catcher. Ugly ratios around him, real counting stats.

bb_waivers_redraft.name: Drake Baldwin
bb_waivers_redraft.why: Braves catcher stream if your C is cold.

bb_waivers_redraft.name: Maikel Garcia
bb_waivers_redraft.why: Steals stream. Do not overthink the batting average.

bb_waivers_redraft.name: Brice Turang
bb_waivers_redraft.why: If he is free, you need speed. That is the whole note.

bb_waivers_redraft.name: Otto Lopez
bb_waivers_redraft.why: The RotoGraphs overperformer. Stream the average.

bb_waivers_redraft.name: Miguel Vargas
bb_waivers_redraft.why: White Sox corner bat. Available, hitting enough.

bb_waivers_redraft.name: Wilyer Abreu
bb_waivers_redraft.why: Boston outfield. Play the home stand.

bb_waivers_redraft.name: Randy Arozarena
bb_waivers_redraft.why: If someone cut him after a cold week, that is a gift.

bb_waivers_redraft.name: Jo Adell
bb_waivers_redraft.why: Power stream. Ignore the team, take the homers.

bb_waivers_redraft.name: Heliot Ramos
bb_waivers_redraft.why: Giants outfield counting stats for the stretch.

bb_waivers_redraft.name: Dylan Lee
bb_waivers_redraft.why: SV+H gold. Holds leagues bump him 10 spots.

bb_waivers_redraft.name: Kevin Kelly
bb_waivers_redraft.why: Rays setup. Must-roster in holds, streaming in saves if Baker sits.

bb_waivers_redraft.name: Tyler Rogers
bb_waivers_redraft.why: Submarine holds. The boring add that wins categories.

bb_waivers_redraft.name: Hunter Gaddis
bb_waivers_redraft.why: Cleveland setup behind Cade Smith. SV+H staple.

bb_waivers_redraft.name: Adrian Morejon
bb_waivers_redraft.why: Padres setup. Miller gets saves; Morejon gets the rest.

bb_waivers_redraft.name: Alex Vesia
bb_waivers_redraft.why: Dodger lefty. Holds plus the Diaz/Scott mess.

bb_waivers_redraft.name: Jeremiah Estrada
bb_waivers_redraft.why: Strikeout reliever. Ratios leagues, not just SV+H.

bb_waivers_redraft.name: Garrett Cleavinger
bb_waivers_redraft.why: Rays bullpen is a factory. Roster two of them if you can.

bb_waivers_redraft.name: Jac Caglianone
bb_waivers_redraft.why: Young bat with enough September at-bats to stream.

bb_waivers_redraft.name: Colson Montgomery
bb_waivers_redraft.why: White Sox shortstop. Deep 12s and 15s only.

bb_waivers_redraft.name: Xavier Edwards
bb_waivers_redraft.why: Steals stream. Average is the tax.

bb_waivers_redraft.name: Chandler Simpson
bb_waivers_redraft.why: Speed-only stream. You know what you are doing.

bb_waivers_redraft.name: Casey Mize
bb_waivers_redraft.why: Two-start filler. Check the matchup, then go.

bb_waivers_redraft.name: Nick Lodolo
bb_waivers_redraft.why: Lefty stream. Great park spots only.

bb_waivers_redraft.name: Joe Ryan
bb_waivers_redraft.why: If he hit waivers after one clunker, that is a September mistake.

bb_waivers_redraft.name: Spencer Schwellenbach
bb_waivers_redraft.why: Braves starter stream. Ks if the elbow holds.

bb_waivers_redraft.name: Cade Horton
bb_waivers_redraft.why: Cubs innings. Deep leagues, two-start weeks.

bb_waivers_redraft.name: Trevor Megill
bb_waivers_redraft.why: Still closing in Milwaukee. If dropped, he is priority 1-adjacent.

pl_players.name: Erling Haaland
plus: The Premier 1.01 and Sleeper BPL 1.01 - 27 goals, 317.2 Sleeper points.
First-choice penalties at £15.5m. The published boards still have him inside the top three.
25.5 xG, 27 finishes. The finishing did not run hot. It ran like Haaland.
The Premier 1st overall - hybrid of Sleeper BPL and the published pro lists.
317.2 Sleeper BPL 2025 points (Pitch #1).
minus: £15.5m is the FPL tax. You cannot pair him with two other premiums without wrecking the squad.
Fantasy Football Scout parks him 24th on a value lean - that is the £15.5m talking, not the striker.
Yahoo's GW1 XI has him 10th. Template managers still try to go without the obvious.
8 assists on 2.67 xA - the creation number needs a second season.
Board spread 1–15 (Sleeper BPL 2025 to Premier League Scout Club Picks).
grafs: Erling Haaland is the player The Premier is built around. Sleeper BPL 2025 scored his 2025/26 line at 317.2, first of 400. The other 23 boards average 3.87. Split the difference and he is still 1.01. Twenty-seven Premier League goals, eight assists, 34 starts, 2,953 minutes, 13 clean-sheet cameos that Sleeper barely cares about because he is a forward. The Pitch already had him first. The Premier does not argue.

The 2025/26 tape is the same argument on film: City walk him into the box and he finishes. 25.5 expected goals, 27 actual. That is not a lucky spike. That is a No. 9 doing No. 9 work at a volume nobody else on this list can touch. Igor Thiago's 22 goals are the closest counting-stat rival and still live 60 Sleeper points back because Haaland also added eight assists and a 6.8 FPL points-per-game.

Set pieces are the rest of the floor. He is first-choice from the spot. He is not on corners. He does not need to be. Threat 1,520, ICT 302.3, 43 bonus. Official FPL had him on 239 points, also first. The boards that fade him (Scout 24, SofaScore 17, Yahoo XI 10) are pricing the £15.5m hit or a single-week XI, not the season. We are ranking the season.
£15.5m is the market admitting the 1.01. The Premier's job is not to be clever about Haaland. It is to put him first so the rest of the 400 has a ceiling to be measured against.

Instruction: you do not trade Haaland for two very good players on this curve. Rank 1 is 12,000 BK Value. Bruno at 2 is close enough that a calculator will call some packages fair. The board still wants the Norwegian. If your league scores Sleeper, this is not a conversation. If it scores FPL, it is still not a conversation.

pl_players.name: Bruno Fernandes
plus: Consensus 3.48 - tighter than Haaland's 3.87. Five boards have him 1.01.
24 assists, first-choice pens, corners, and direct free-kicks. The whole dead-ball tree.
293.8 Sleeper, Pitch #2. The creation 1.01 on a board that still ranks the No. 9 first.
The Premier 2nd overall - hybrid of Sleeper BPL and the published pro lists.
293.8 Sleeper BPL 2025 points (Pitch #2).
minus: Turns 32 this season. The Athletic has him 12th - the first age tax on a midfielder who plays every week.
Seven clean sheets as a midfielder. United's defensive tape still caps the CS crumbs Sleeper pays at 1.
£12.0m. You are paying a second premium after Haaland.
24 assists on 12.28 xA - the creation number needs a second season.
Board spread 1–16 (FPL ICT Index to Premier League Scout Club Picks).
grafs: Bruno Fernandes is the midfielder every board still refuses to fade. Fantasy Football Fix, Yahoo's cheat sheet, ESPN, WhoScored, and the ICT index all had him first. Sleeper BPL 2025 had him second, 293.8, because 24 assists at 6 points each is how a creator outranks almost every goalscorer who is not Haaland. The Premier averages that into #2. Consensus 3.48 versus Haaland's 3.87 - the industry actually likes Bruno more. Production likes Haaland more. We split it and keep the Norwegian first by a hair.

The 2025/26 line is 9 goals, 24 assists, 35 starts, 3,065 minutes, 10.79 xG, 12.28 xA. He slightly under-finished the shot map and still ended as FPL's second-highest scorer (235). First-choice penalties, first-choice corners, first-choice direct free-kicks. Fifty-three tackles and 67 CBI are the part of the profile FPL undervalues and Sleeper does not. That is why his Sleeper rank (2) beats several of the 'he's just a creator' boards.

United are not a clean-sheet machine (7 CS, 46 goals against while he was on). Sleeper pays midfielders 1 for a clean sheet, so the defensive mess is a rounding error, not a ranking event. The real minus is age. He is 31. The Athletic sliding him to 12 is the 'how many more 90s?' question. We hear it. We are not moving him out of the first two for it.

Price is £12.0m. That is the second-most expensive shirt on the app for a reason. Scout's 14 is the value lean talking. Ignore value leans when the player takes every set piece and 24 chances. The Premier is not an FPL budget tool. It is a ranking of who actually produced and who the industry still believes.

Nearby on this list is Semenyo at 3, then Gabriel. If you need to move Bruno, the package starts with a top-five name, not a pair of mid-premiums. Draft-league managers who still think 'United midfielder' means a tax can be the other side of that trade. Take Bruno. Stop talking.

pl_players.name: Bukayo Saka
plus: Consensus 18.1 versus Sleeper 32. The industry still believes the player more than last year's counting line.
7 G, 10 A, £10.0m-class usage, Arsenal's right side. The name has not gone anywhere.
Premier 16 is a buy versus Pitch 32 - this is exactly what the third list is for.
The Premier 3rd overall - hybrid of Sleeper BPL and the published pro lists.
182.2 Sleeper BPL 2025 points (Pitch #32).
minus: 182.2 Sleeper from a player people still treat as a 1.03. The 2025/26 volume was not 2023 Saka.
If the minutes were the injury year, fine. If they were the new baseline, the consensus is behind.
Paying Saka prices for 7-and-10 is how premium midfielders become dead cap.
Board spread 2–44 (RotoWire GW1 captains to FPL Ownership).
grafs: Bukayo Saka is the first big 'industry versus box score' test on The Premier. Sleeper BPL 2025 had him 32nd (182.2) on 7 goals and 10 assists. The other boards average 18.1 because he is still Bukayo Saka in an Arsenal shirt. Hybrid 16. We are not putting him back in the first five on brand. We are not leaving him at 32 on a down year as if the player changed nationality.

The 2025/26 line is the honest one: the returns dipped, the name did not. Ten assists keep him in the creator band. Seven goals do not keep him in the Semenyo band. The Premier's job is to split that. Sixteen is 'still a first-round FPL name, not a first-round Sleeper name.' Draft him like the first. Pay him like the second if someone is still offering 2023 prices.

Arsenal's attack has Rice, set pieces, and a centre-forward committee. Saka is no longer the only way the ball finds the box. That is the structural minus. The plus is he is still the one defenders game-plan. Consensus 18 says the experts did not resign. Sleeper 32 says the season did.

Instruction: buy the gap. If a manager has him outside the top 25 because of 7 goals, that is the trade. If a manager still wants Haaland-adjacent capital, cash it. Premier 16 is the number we will defend.

Bukayo Saka is a midfielder for Arsenal, age 24, £9.5m. The Premier ranks him 3rd overall by splitting Sleeper BPL 2025 (#32, 182.2 points) with the consensus of 13 other boards (5.77). The industry still has him 26 spots ahead of the 2025/26 Sleeper count. The Premier pays that reputation something, not everything. Brand does not outrun a down year, and a down year does not erase a player Arsenal still builds around.

plus: Sleeper DEF1 (258.6) on 18 clean sheets, 3 goals, 5 assists, 239 CBI.

Arsenal's back line is the clean-sheet engine. 20 goals against in 2,750 minutes.
The Premier 4th overall - hybrid of Sleeper BPL and the published pro lists.
258.6 Sleeper BPL 2025 points (Pitch #3).
minus: xGI board has him 107th - Sleeper and FPL attacking-contribution ranks do not love a centre-back.
ICT 80th. The 'he doesn't dribble' tax on a player whose job is not to dribble.
28 years old, £8.0m. You are paying defender-premium for a season that already happened.
5 assists on 1.75 xA - the creation number needs a second season.
Board spread 1–107 (Premier League Scout Club Picks to FPL xGI).
grafs: Gabriel Magalhães is why The Premier exists as a third list. Sleeper BPL 2025 had him third overall, 258.6, because an Arsenal centre-back with 18 clean sheets, 3 goals, 5 assists, 38 tackles, and 239 clearances/blocks/interceptions is a cheat code in a scoring system that pays 6 for a CS and 0.4 per CBI. The FPL-shaped boards average him 12.78. Hybrid lands at 4. That gap is the whole methodology: production said 3, the industry said 13, we are not throwing either number away.

The 2025/26 line is 30 starts, 2,750 minutes, 209 FPL points (third overall), 6.5 PPG, 30 bonus. 2.94 xG and 3 goals - no finishing luck. 1.75 xA and 5 assists - he over-created a bit from set-piece chaos, which Arsenal will keep manufacturing. SofaScore and the Scout value lean both had him 1.01 because they watch defenders. The xGI table had him 107th because it does not.

£8.0m is the market catching up without fully arriving. Saliba and Calafiori live in the same building and do not outrank him here. Sleeper is not confused about which centre-back got on the ball in the box and also blocked everything.

The minus is architectural: if Arsenal's clean-sheet rate drops, a lot of these points are not replaceable with 'he will just score more.' He scored 3. The floor is the defending. The Premier is willing to take that floor in the first four because last year's floor was a top-three season in two different scoring systems.

Instruction: do not trade Gabriel for a midfielder who 'feels more premium' unless that midfielder is Bruno or Semenyo. Draft formats that pay CBI and CS will scream if you do. FPL managers who still think £8.0 is 'too much for a defender' are the other side of the trade. Take the Brazilian.

grafs: Antoine Semenyo is the first name The Premier is willing to argue about. Sleeper had him fifth (247.6) on 17 goals and 6 assists from midfield. The other boards average 6.14. The 2025/26 counting line is a feature-winger season: 37 starts, 3,200 minutes, 17 G, 6 A, 12 clean sheets (Sleeper pays mids 1), 45 tackles. FPL had him on 202 points, fourth overall. Price is £8.5m. xGI rank 11 and EP-next 12 are the FPL app still treating him like a Bournemouth winger. The Pitch already moved. The Premier moved with it. The public has not finished the sentence 'he plays for City now.'

Yellows (7) and third-choice pens are the minuses that do not move a ranking this high. He is not Bruno. He does not need to be. He is the midfielder who scores like a forward and now shares a building with the actual 1.01. City can make that a problem (minutes) or a cheat code (box entries). 37 starts last year says he survives minutes fights.

Instruction: if your league still has him priced like a Bournemouth output, that is a buy. If someone wants Haaland-lite and offers a top-eight package, listen.
